data.name: Orchard Row
data.summary: Nine family homes on the site of an old orchard, each with a garden and a tall gable that lets light into the stairs.
data.story: The co-operative wanted homes their members could afford to heat. The terrace faces south across the old orchard, so every living room gets the low winter sun, and the walls are thick enough that most houses need the heating on only in the coldest weeks. We kept eleven of the pear trees and planted the rest of the gardens with the members on two Saturdays.
data.imageAlt: A terrace of brick houses with tall gables and white doors behind a green lawn

data.name: Riverside Library
data.summary: A long reading room on a stone plinth by the river, open from eight in the morning until nine at night.
data.story: The old library sat behind a car park. The new one turns its long side to the water: a timber room on a stone base that floods safely in the spring, with the children’s library at the end that catches the morning sun. The plinth is built from stone of the warehouse that stood here before.
data.imageAlt: A long timber-clad building with a dark glazed reading room on a stone plinth beside a river

data.name: Ropewalk Studios
data.summary: A Victorian rope warehouse turned into twenty workshops for furniture makers, under a new glass roof.
data.story: The brick walls were sound; the roof had gone. We put a steel and glass roof on the old walls, opened the arched doors again and divided the long floor into workshops of three sizes that share one machine room. The rope makers’ iron rings are still in the walls.
data.imageAlt: An old red-brick warehouse with arched doors under a new pitched glass roof

data.name: Hillside House
data.summary: A low concrete house dug into a slope, with one long window looking down the valley.
data.story: The planners wanted nothing seen from the ridge path, and the family wanted the view. The house is set into the hill so the grass runs over its back, and the one window at the front is as long as the house. The concrete was poured with lime from the next valley, which gives it its warm colour.
data.imageAlt: A low pale house set into a green hillside with one long window, the sun above

data.name: Market Hall Canopy
data.summary: A folded timber roof over the market square, so the Saturday market can run in any weather.
data.story: Three slender rows of columns carry a roof folded like paper, high enough for a delivery van underneath and low enough to keep the rain off the stalls. The roof is on; the last bay is under scaffolding, and the square opens again in the spring.
data.imageAlt: A folded wooden roof on thin columns over market stalls, with yellow scaffolding at one end

data.name: Courtyard School
data.summary: Six new classrooms in two wings around a planted courtyard, each with its own door to the garden.
data.story: The school grew from one class a year to two. Rather than build up, we wrapped the playground with two low wings, so every classroom opens straight onto the courtyard and the youngest children never use a stair. The courtyard is where the school now holds its assemblies in summer.
data.imageAlt: Seen from above, two low classroom wings around a green courtyard with three trees and a path
